# Clue shapes

<!-- CLUE_SHAPES-START generated by tools/clue_shapes.py: do not edit -->

Every annotated clue's wordplay tree reduced to a skeleton (op tree, leaves abstracted to a type), over 556,644 clues in 58,214 puzzles: 19,979 distinct skeletons, folded into coarser groups below. Generated by `tools/clue_shapes.py` (`nice -n 19 python3 tools/clue_shapes.py`, about five minutes); the judgements come from `tools/data/clue_shape_verdicts.json`, which the tool never writes.

Leaf types: **V** verbatim clue words (and any fodder under an anagram, hidden or selection op), **F** folded (`gives` is part of the words, or the words part of `gives`: a link word, indicator or selection swallowed by the leaf), **A** one or two letters from other words (abbreviation, symbol), **S** synonym or other `gives`, **B** bare letters with no clue words, **U** unchecked leaf. `?` after an op name means its node is unchecked. Definition key: `2d` is the number of definitions, then where each sits (S start, E end, W whole clue, M middle); `&lit` when andLit is set.

Ops: the name the tables and prose use, and how it is written in a skeleton or tree. A charade is written `(a+b)` everywhere, in skeletons and in tier-2 trees alike.

| name | written | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| charade | `(a+b)` | the parts placed one after another |
| anagram | `ana` | the fodder letters rearranged |
| reversal | `rev` | the letters read backwards |
| container | `ins` | one part goes inside another |
| deletion | `del` | letters removed from a word |
| hidden word | `hid` | the answer sits inside the clue words |
| homophone | `sound` | sounds like the answer |
| spoonerism | `spoon` | initial sounds swapped |
| substitution | `sub` | one letter or part swapped for another |
| cycling | `cyc` | letters rotated |
| cryptic definition | `cdef` | the whole clue is one misleading definition |
| rebus | `rebus` | a picture of letters |
| composite anagram | `comp` | one anagram shared across several fodders |
| reverse clue | `reverse` | the wordplay and definition roles are flipped |
| palindrome | `pal` | reads the same both ways |
| first letters | `first` | the first letter(s) of the fodder |
| last letters | `last` | the last letter(s) of the fodder |
| middle letters | `mid` | the middle letter(s) of the fodder |
| outer letters | `outer` | the outer letters of the fodder |
| alternate letters | `alt` | alternate letters of the fodder |
| regular letters | `reg` | letters at a regular interval |
| nth letter | `nth` | the nth letter of the fodder |
| letter selection | `select` | any of first, last, mid, outer, alt, reg, nth: one op in tier 1 and in the families |
| double definition | `DD` | two definitions and no wordplay |

## Three ways to group the shapes

The skeleton (tier 3) keeps charade order and arity and every leaf type, so there are thousands. Two coarser groupings sit above it; each is computed from the skeleton, so the verdicts still key on tier 3, and the full skeleton tables further down stay as the place to look for errors.

- **Tier 1, mechanism set**: which ops other than the charade the clue uses, in any number and nesting, named as in the legend above. The letter selections (`first last mid outer alt reg nth`) count as one op, letter selection; a clue with more than 3 different ops is one group; `charade only` is a clue with no other op.
- **Tier 2, mechanism tree**: the op nesting, ops written by their abbreviation, with each leaf (any type) written `x`, siblings sorted and deduplicated so order and arity vanish, a charade that is only leaves written `x`, and a charade of ops written `(a+b)` style at the top of the tree, e.g. `(x+ins(x,x))` (a charade that merely builds one operand of an op is dropped). `ins(ana(x),x)` (an anagram put inside a container) and `ana(ins(x))` (an anagram of a container) stay distinct. A tree of more than 3 op nodes is one group, `4+ ops`. Definition placement is dropped.
- **Tier 3, skeleton**: the exact skeleton, as in the tables further down.

| tier | groups | cover 50% | cover 90% | cover 99% | groups with one clue |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 mechanism set | 112 | 4 | 13 | 30 | 11 |
| 2 mechanism tree | 676 | 4 | 23 | 105 | 206 |
| 3 skeleton | 19,979 | 16 | 834 | 14413 | 12,133 |

## Skeletons with no verdict yet

None: every skeleton of at least 150 clues has a verdict.

## Still being fixed

12,242 clues (2.20%) have a skeleton judged other than ok, in 13 groups, ranked by clues. These are errors in the repair queue (`tools/data/shape_reannotate.json`), not a standing statistic; the list shrinks to None as the queue drains. `right` is the shape the clue should have.

### 1. unchecked node (parse not verified): 4,672 clues (0.84%), unverified

- why: an op or leaf the validator could not rebuild step by step; its letters are taken as filed, so nothing says the shape is real (spoonerisms, cyclings, substitutions, reversals of part of a word and indirect anagrams are most of them)
- right: re-annotate so every step is checked; none can be added now (the ratchet)
- 1539 skeletons; commonest `del?(S)` (437)
  - `times-14078#2d` Brown appears in the pentateuch (UMBER) = `del<appears in>([the pentateuch]NUMBERS)`
  - `times-15746#21a` Fibre revealed by a nocturnal painter (ISTLE) = `del<revealed by>([a nocturnal painter]WHISTLER)`
  - `times-18804#27a` Crime where beheading would be the judgement (TREASON) = `del<beheading>([the judgement]REASON)`

### 2. indirect anagram (fodder is a synonym): 1,684 clues (0.30%), rare

- why: the anagram's fodder is another word's synonym, which only Azed, Mephisto and a few toughies expect solvers to find; in daily puzzles it is an error unless the clue flags it, and in many of these the leaf has simply respelled the printed words
- right: ana(V) over the printed words when the leaf only dropped a link word or respelled; a deliberate indirect anagram stays
- 98 skeletons; commonest `ana(S)` (1,065)
  - `times-21#5d` Jurisprudence may here be jumbled but there's still point in it. (AWL) = `ana<jumbled>([Jurisprudence]LAW)`
  - `times-13685#24d` Flower — perhaps sown by an enemy ? (ASTER) = `ana<perhaps>([sown by an enemy]TARES)`
  - `times-13843#26a` What Sheffield would be if it turned loose (UNTIED) = `ana<turned>([What Sheffield would be]UNITED)`

### 3. same letter selection repeated word by word: 1,640 clues (0.29%), redundant

- why: an acrostic (heads of each word, tails, middles) built as one op per word inside a charade, usually with the indicator on the first op only, where the clue means one pick across a phrase
- right: one first/last/mid/outer/nth op over a single multi-word leaf
- 324 skeletons; commonest `(mid(V)+mid(V)+mid(V))` (156)
  - `times-16622#21d` Centre-halves with ball kick leaning forwards (ITALIC) = `(mid<Centre-halves>([with]) + mid([ball]) + mid([kick]))`
  - `times-20141#14d` Vines clasp stick, all their centres becoming rigid (INELASTIC) = `(mid<all their centres>([Vines]) + mid([clasp]) + mid([stick]))`
  - `times-20186#23a` Contents of home sad chap assembled in US city (OMAHA) = `(mid<Contents of>([home]) + mid([sad]) + mid([chap]))`

### 4. letter selection from a synonym: 1,295 clues (0.23%), rare

- why: an initial, ending or middle taken from a synonym rather than from the clue's own words is a hard Azed/Mephisto device; in the daily papers these are almost all a fodder leaf that swallowed the indicator or a link word ('[Cameron's first]CAMERONFIRST')
- right: sel(V) over exactly the fodder words; the indicator belongs on the op
- 251 skeletons; commonest `mid(S)` (625)
  - `times-16647#12a` Three characters central to the sequel to "Kidnapped" (TRIO) = `mid<characters central to>([the sequel to "Kidnapped"]CATRIONA)`
  - `times-19460#17a` It occurs in the midst of our Biblical span (EVENT) = `mid<in the midst of>([our Biblical span]SEVENTY)`
  - `times-20013#24d` Passage through middle of Scottish town (AISLE) = `mid<middle of>([Scottish town]PAISLEY)`

### 5. wordplay that is one synonym leaf: 752 clues (0.14%), mislabelled

- why: a tree of a single leaf is no wordplay at all: it restates the answer as one 'synonym' of the clue words, or is a cross-reference ('See 1')
- right: a cryptic definition, a double definition, or a real parse; a cross-reference belongs to the linked group
- 4 skeletons; commonest `S` (724)
  - `times-13807#9a` Property in Maryland, for instance ? (ESTATE) = `[Maryland, for instance]ESTATE`
  - `times-14094#13a` Extension of the batsman's position? (INCREASE) = `[batsman's position]INCREASE`
  - `times-14220#6d` Palmy firms (COCO) = `[firms]COCO`

### 6. four or more mechanisms in one clue: 624 clues (0.11%), rare

- why: four non-charade ops (nested containers with deletions and reversals, long acrostics) is more than a solver can unpick from a clue; real setters stop at two, occasionally three; the commonest are acrostics, double containers around acrostics, and one deletion written letter by letter, del(del(del(..))), that is really one op (an op nested four deep always lands here, so there is no separate depth rule)
- right: fewer ops: merge repeated selections, flatten containers, or check the parse
- 517 skeletons; commonest `ins(ana(del(V,B)),del((A+A),B))` (14)
  - `times-27500#25a` Hoping to relieve pressure, cooked around 200 dumplings (GNOCCHI) = `ins<around>(ana<cooked>(del<to relieve>([Hoping], P)), del(([pressure]P + [200]CC), P))`
  - `independent-12076#28a` Poor lady's not one that is included in profits (YIELDS) = `ins<included in>(ana<Poor>(del<not>([lady's], A)), del(([one]A + [that is]IE), A))`
  - `everyman-3583#8d` Mostly excited, having time off, receiving book token (SYMBOL) = `ins<receiving>(ana<excited>(del<off>([Mostly], T)), del(([time]T + [book]B), T))`

### 7. anagram wrapped around a container: 563 clues (0.10%), mislabelled

- why: the anagram is stored outside the container, as the last step, but the clues work the other way: a synonym or word is the container and an anagram of clue words goes inside it (FLYPITCH: LYP, an anagram of 'ply', inside FITCH, 'fur'; SECRETARIATE: CRETA, an anagram of 'crate', inside SERIATE). Almost all are unchecked, so nothing refused the wrong nesting
- right: ins(outer, ana(V)): the anagram is the container's inner arm
- 75 skeletons; commonest `ana(ins(S,V))` (156)
  - `times-13777#14a` Unusual mine: get one who knows to come round to test (EXPERIMENT) = `ana<Unusual>(ins<to come round>([one who knows]EXPERT, [mine]))`
  - `times-14043#5a` Weapon brings terrible evil within a month (JAVELIN) = `ana<terrible>(ins<within>([a month]JAN, [evil]))`
  - `times-14521#16d` In certain circumstances cling madly to the girth (SURCINGLE) = `ana<madly>(ins<In><circumstances>([certain]SURE, [cling]))`

### 8. answer letters with no clue words in a charade: 537 clues (0.10%), mislabelled

- why: a charade piece (or fodder piece) made of letters no clue word supplies: an unexplained gap in the parse, not a mechanism
- right: the leaf for the clue word that supplies them (an abbreviation or a selection)
- 330 skeletons; commonest `(B+S)` (38)
  - `cryptic-22231#22a` Don't take away food for plant hormone (ZEATIN) = `(Z + [Don't take away food]EATIN)`
  - `azed-2209#15d` One uttering shrill cry (animal by the sound of it?) (CREECHER) = `(S + [animal by the sound of it]CREECHER)`
  - `genius-1#10a` Busy bird (ATIT) = `(A + [bird]TIT)`

### 9. reversal and anagram stacked: 329 clues (0.06%), redundant

- why: an anagram's output order is free, so reversing it (or anagramming a reversal) adds nothing; in these clues the reverse indicator really sits on a different piece, or the intermediate word is an invented string
- right: one anagram over the fodder, with the reversal on its own sibling piece if there is one
- 134 skeletons; commonest `(rev(ana(V))+rev(S))` (26)
  - `times-14080#12a` Here water supply is pivotal; has reformed nourishment in return (SHADOOF) = `(rev<in return>(ana<reformed>([has])) + rev([nourishment]FOOD))`
  - `cryptic-25794#14a` Tethering tiny mongrel, rebellious little dog (TYINGUP) = `(rev<rebellious>(ana([tiny])) + rev([little dog]PUG))<mongrel>`
  - `independent-10336#3d` Artfully hide returning fat with particular angle (DIHEDRAL) = `(rev<returning>(ana<Artfully>([hide])) + rev([fat]LARD))`

### 10. anagram of a charade of verbatim words: 59 clues (0.01%), redundant

- why: the fodder is cut into word-by-word leaves joined by an unindicated charade, which says nothing a single multi-word fodder leaf does not; the charade is not a mechanism here, it is the fodder written in pieces
- right: ana(V): one leaf holding all the fodder words
- 6 skeletons; commonest `ana((V+V))` (48)
  - `times-28440#18a` Fearful priest facing Ely's crumbling stonework (PERISTYLES) = `ana<Fearful><crumbling>(([priest] + [Ely's]))`
  - `cryptic-21804#9a` An odd escort for an older member of the family! (ANCESTOR) = `ana<odd>(([An] + [escort]))`
  - `independent-8343#2d` A girl carelessly chasing a sheep (ARGALI) = `ana<carelessly>(([a] + [A girl])<chasing>)`

### 11. letter selection over another selection or op: 46 clues (0.01%), implausible

- why: a pick made from the result of another operation (first of the outer letters, first of the middle); a setter writes one selection, so this is a two-step the clue does not print, or a leaf that swallowed an indicator
- right: one selection op over the fodder words, or the picks as separate pieces of a charade
- 23 skeletons; commonest `first?(alt?(U))` (6)
  - `cryptic-26842#7d` * Essential oil for bosom, even? (OTTO) = `first<even>(alt([bosom]OO))`

### 12. charade directly inside a charade: 23 clues (0.00%), redundant

- why: a charade is associative, so a bracketed charade inside a charade changes nothing; most carry a trailing unchecked leaf of leftover words
- right: one flat charade (or an indicator on the whole charade)
- 22 skeletons; commonest `ana?(((A+V)+U))` (2)
  - `cryptic-27057#1d` Note added to unusual tune for dance (MINUET) = `ana<unusual>((([Note]MI + [tune]) + [added to]))`
  - `genius-95#20d` Artist losing turn off busy road (RATRUN) = `ana<off>((([Artist]RA + [turn]) + [losing]))`

### 13. palindrome with its definition or indicator stored as leaves: 18 clues (0.00%), mislabelled

- why: the palindrome op wraps unchecked leaves that are the definition and the indicator rather than letters
- right: pal<indicator>([fodder]) or pal() over the answer alone
- 2 skeletons; commonest `pal(U)` (16)
  - `times-14520#12a` Look both ways (PEEP) = `pal<both ways>([Look])`
  - `cryptic-22397#11a` Something done both ways (DEED) = `pal<both ways>([Something done])`
  - `quiptic-65#11a` Reversible doctrine (TENET) = `pal<Reversible>([doctrine])`

Notes on the commonest:

- `DD`: a double definition: two definitions, no wordplay, the one family with no tree
- `ana(V)`: the plain anagram of clue words
- `(S+S)`: the plain charade of two synonyms
- `del(S,B)`: the removed letters are stored bare (no clue words), as a head, tail or inner deletion of a few letters; legitimate, but a positional deletion (first/last letter) carries its meaning only in the indicator
